requested.title: Duplicate query parameters crash the hydrated island on the page this route serves
Published demo source omits shared.ts, leaving parseTransition/TRANSITIONS undefined and a dangling './shared' import

rawResponses.rawText:
```json
[
  {
    "findingId": "F1",
    "verdict": "true-positive",
    "adjustedSeverity": "BUG",
    "reasoning": "I verified every link in the chain from source. `packages/site/src/demos/url/routes.ts:5` mounts `Url.svelte`, which is spread into the live site's route map (`packages/site/src/routes.ts:83` + `:410`), and `Url.svelte:13-15` renders `UrlInfo` twice — once plain (SSR-only) and once with `mochi:hydrate`. `UrlInfo.svelte:9` does `[...url.searchParams]`, and line 31 is `{#each getParams() as [key, value] (key)}` — keyed on the parameter *name*. On the server, `url` resolves through `__mochiCtxProxy('url')` (`compiler/virtual-modules/mochi-env.server.js:27`) to the request context's `URL` built by `buildPublicUrl` (`runtime/requestSetup.ts:89`), which preserves the query string verbatim; on the client it resolves to `new URL(window.location.href)` (`mochi-env.client.js:24-37`). So both renders see two entries for `?name=a&name=b`. I confirmed the Svelte 5.57.3 SSR transform (`compiler/phases/3-transform/server/visitors/EachBlock.js`) ignores `node.key` entirely — a plain `for` loop with no validation — and that `each_key_duplicate` exists only under `internal/client/`, so SSR emits both rows and returns 200. On the client, `internal/client/dom/blocks/each.js:356-363` runs `if (length > keys.size)` unconditionally (including on the first, hydrating run — I traced the function from line 267 and the check sits after the loop with no `hydrating`/`DEV` guard), and the non-DEV branch calls `e.each_key_duplicate('', '', '')`, which `internal/client/errors.js:145-147` throws in production too. I also confirmed the key function is generated as `([key, value]) => key` (`client/visitors/EachBlock.js:296-306`), so the two rows genuinely collide. The error propagates synchronously: `create_effect` re-throws (`reactivity/effects.js:137-142`), the root boundary created by `_mount` has only `{pending}` — no `failed`/`onerror` — so `Boundary.error()` re-throws (`boundary.js:473-476`), and it lands in `HydratableIsland._doHydrate`'s try/catch (`web-components/HydratableIsland.ts:56-65`), which logs and appends a `<mochi-island-failure>` stub (hidden in production by `ISLAND_FAILURE_CSS`). Attack/trigger is trivially concrete: any visitor following a link to `/demos/url/?name=a&name=b` (or any duplicated tracking param) on a page whose own copy invites `?name=mochi`. Two small corrections to the finding: the containment actually comes from the island hydrating inside its own custom element with a try/catch (the page itself is never hydrated, so the preprocessor's `<svelte:boundary>` is SSR-only here), and because `create_effect`/`destroy_effect` unwind the subtree the island's server HTML is likely torn down rather than left intact beside a stub — either way the failure is island-scoped, not a page crash. The finding is also anchored on `routes.ts` while the defect is in `UrlInfo.svelte:9,31`, which it states plainly and its recommendation targets correctly. File is unmodified since commit 11bbbe6b, so not fixed. BUG severity is right: no security impact, no DoS, but a real reachable correctness bug.",
    "verdict_note": null
  },
  {
    "findingId": "F2",
    "verdict": "true-positive",
    "adjustedSeverity": "BUG",
    "reasoning": "Confirmed on both halves, by reading the full chain rather than the flagged lines. `view-transitions/files.ts` lists PageOne, PageTwo, TransitionCard, PersistentVideo, persistent.js, routes.ts and demoIndex.ts — no `shared.ts` — while `view-transitions/shared.ts` exports `TRANSITIONS`, `TransitionType`, `parseTransition`, `description` and a re-exported `sources`. That list is the single source of truth for both consumers: `sources.prerender.ts` calls `loadSources(files)`, which runs each file through `stripDemoWrapper` (`components/utils.ts:23,73`), and `lib/docs.ts:213` (`buildDemoLlmsTxt` via `filesForDemo`, `docs.ts:25`) builds `/demos/view-transitions/llms.txt`, which also backs the public `/mcp` `get_section` tool (`lib/mcp.ts:57`). Half 1: `TransitionCard.svelte` has no `import DemoPage from` line, so `stripDemoWrapper` returns early at `utils.ts:74-76` and the tab is published verbatim with `import { TRANSITIONS, type TransitionType } from './shared';` pointing at a file that appears in no tab and no llms.txt section. Half 2: PageOne/PageTwo do have the `DemoPage` import, so the regex at `utils.ts:83` deletes the whole `import { description, sources, parseTransition } from './shared';` line (I hand-traced the regex: `[^}]*` cannot cross a `}`, so it matches only the `./shared` line, not the earlier braced imports), while `utils.ts:84` strips the `<DemoPage …>` wrapper and its `{description}`/`{sources}` attributes — leaving `const type = parseTransition(url.searchParams.get('type'));` in the published script with no import and no definition anywhere in the set. The sibling control checks out exactly as described: `custom-transitions/files.ts:7` does publish `shared.ts`, and its PageOne imports only `{ description, sources }`, so stripping that line leaves compilable code. The `../../components/ViewTransitionFirefoxNote.svelte` import is indeed unpublished in both demos (TransitionCard.svelte:3 and SpinCard.svelte:2), so that one is a consistent site-chrome convention, not the defect. `lib/demoRegistry.test.ts` only asserts slug/files presence and folder registration — nothing checks self-containment, so nothing catches this. One nuance the finding slightly overstates: `buildDemoLlmsTxt` reads raw file text and never calls `stripDemoWrapper`, so llms.txt/`/mcp` consumers see PageOne *with* its `./shared` import but without the module it names — an unresolvable import rather than a literally undefined symbol; the on-page source tabs are where `parseTransition` is called with no visible import. Correctly non-security (static literal paths, no secrets in the omitted file, and `loadSources` only reads paths declared in the registry). The author's `shared.ts` comment says the file is meant to be hidden, so the right fix may be to move the real API (`parseTransition`/`TRANSITIONS`) out of the plumbing module rather than simply publishing it — but either way the published set is objectively not self-contained, so BUG stands.",
    "verdict_note": null
  }
]
```

**Summary:** both findings are confirmed true positives at BUG severity.

- **F1** — verified end-to-end against Svelte 5.57.3's own source: the SSR `EachBlock` transform discards the key (plain `for` loop, no validation), `each_key_duplicate` lives only in the client runtime, and the `length > keys.size` check at `each.js:356-363` is unconditional with the non-DEV branch still throwing (`errors.js:145`). A repeated query parameter on `/demos/url/` therefore SSRs cleanly and then throws on hydration. Two mechanism corrections: containment comes from `HydratableIsland._doHydrate`'s try/catch (the page is never hydrated, so the preprocessor boundary is SSR-only), and the island's server DOM is likely torn down by effect unwinding rather than left beside a stub. Still island-scoped, not a page crash.

- **F2** — both halves verified. `TransitionCard.svelte` is published verbatim (early return at `utils.ts:74`) with a dangling `./shared` import; PageOne/PageTwo have that import stripped by `utils.ts:83` while still calling `parseTransition(...)`. `custom-transitions/files.ts:7` is a genuine control. One imprecision: `buildDemoLlmsTxt` never applies `stripDemoWrapper`, so llms.txt/`/mcp` consumers get an unresolvable import rather than a literally undefined symbol — the undefined-symbol case is the on-page source tabs.
